Home > Deck Building Operations

Deck Building Operations

Adding Cards

  • Fastest Method: Switch to your desired deck tab on the right, find the card in the Master List, and double-click it.
  • Drag and Drop: Left-click and drag the card from the Master List onto any visible tab list.
  • Targeted Right-Click: Right-click a card in the Master List, open the Copy submenu, and pick the destination tab (Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, Sites). This automatically switches focus to that tab.

Duplicating Cards

To add another copy of a card already in a deck tab, simply double-click it directly within that tab's list.

Moving Cards Between Tabs

  1. Right-click the card inside any deck tab.
  2. Highlight Move.
  3. Select the destination tab. The card is added to the target tab and removed from the current tab.

Deleting Cards

  • Right-click the card in the deck tab and select Delete.

Context Menu Reference (Deck Tabs)

Menu Item Action
[Card Name Header] Shows card title in the active header color.
Copy Duplicates card to Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, or Sites.
Move Transfers card to another tab and removes it from current tab.
Delete Permanently removes this copy from the current tab.
Card Attributes Displays a monospace readout of all official database attributes for this card.
Assigned Tags Shows user-defined tags currently assigned to this card.
Assign Tag Assigns or reassigns a custom tag to this card (active tag is checkmarked), creates a new tag in an existing category, or authors a new category and tag.
Remove Tag Removes an assigned custom tag from this card (only visible if the card currently has custom tags assigned; does not delete the tag from your taxonomy).

Home > Saving & Exporting

Saving & Export Formats

Native Deck Files (.json)

Use File > Save or File > Open (Ctrl+O) to store and load complete deck configurations in native JSON format. This preserves:

  • The full contents of all 5 tabs (Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, Sites).
  • Active set selections.
  • Deck title.

Export Options (File > Export / Ctrl+S)

Choose File > Export to open the export dialog and select from the dropdown filter:

Format Extension Target Platform & Usage
Tabletop Simulator .json Generates five JSON deck files (one for each section: _pool.json, _resource.json, _hazard.json, _sideboard.json, _site.json) ready to be dropped into Tabletop Simulator's Saved Objects folder.
Play MECCG .play Standard export for the online Play MECCG client. Formats cards with parenthetical subtitle convention (e.g. Adrazar (TW)) using Windows-1252 ANSI encoding.
Cardnum Deck .cnum Exports deck listings using standard Cardnum code prefixes (e.g. 1 Adrazar (TW)) grouped by deck sections.
Archive Listing .archive A structured analysis format that breaks down your deck by category: Items (Minor, Major, Greater, Ring), Events (Short, Long, Permanent), Allies, Factions, Characters by race, and Sites by type.
Text File .txt A clean, human-readable plain text breakdown of all deck sections with section headers.

Home > Overview

MECCG Deck Builder

MECCG Deck Builder is a dedicated Windows desktop application designed to build, organize, filter, and export decks for the Middle-earth Collectible Card Game (MECCG) published by Iron Crown Enterprises (I.C.E.), including official expansions and player council Dreamcard sets.

Key Capabilities

  • Live Data Integration: Synchronizes cards and expansion sets from the Cardnum open database, with seamless local offline JSON fallbacks.
  • On-Demand Image Preview & Caching: Displays high-resolution card artwork downloaded on demand and cached locally to conserve bandwidth.
  • Five-Section Deck Partitioning: Organizes cards into standard MECCG deck sections: Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, and Sites.
  • Dual Filtering Engine: Filter the card catalog simultaneously by official Cardnum metadata (race, skills, items, alignments) and customizable user-defined tags.
  • Multi-Platform Exporting: Directly export decks to Tabletop Simulator (TTS), Play MECCG online client, Cardnum list format, structured text archives, or plain text lists.

Quick Start Guide

  1. Select Card Sets: Click Set in the top menu bar to check the expansions you want to browse (defaults to The Wizards).
  2. Filter Cards: Use the dropdown menus at the bottom left to filter by card properties (such as Primary = Character, Race = Dúnadan).
  3. Add Cards to Your Deck:
    • Double-click any card in the Master List to add it to the active tab on the right.
    • Or drag and drop cards directly into any deck tab.
    • Or right-click a card in the Master List and choose Copy > [Target Tab].
  4. Review Title Bar Counters: Watch the window title update dynamically with card counts: MECCG Deck Builder - "DeckName" (Pool/Resources[Characters]/Hazards/Sideboard/Sites).
  5. Save or Export: Choose File > Save to keep your deck in native JSON format, or File > Export to generate files for Tabletop Simulator or Play MECCG.

Home > Interface Walkthrough

User Interface Walkthrough

The application interface is divided into four main functional zones:

1. Master Card List (Left Pane)

The left listbox displays all available cards matching your selected sets and active filter criteria, sorted alphabetically.

  • Single-Click: Selects the card and loads its image into the central preview panel.
  • Double-Click: Immediately appends the card to the currently selected deck tab on the right.
  • Right-Click: Opens the master context menu to copy the card into a specific deck tab, inspect its official Card Attributes, view Assigned Tags, or assign custom tags.
  • Drag & Drop: Left-click and hold to drag the card title onto any deck listbox.

2. Card Image Preview (Center Pane)

Displays a high-resolution preview of the selected card. Images are downloaded automatically from cardnum.net upon first selection and saved into a local folder named after the card set (e.g., METW/, MEDM/).

Errata Notice: Cards flagged with ICE errata automatically load their corrected image counterpart prefixed with ice-.

3. Deck Tabs (Right Pane)

The right pane features five tabbed lists representing standard MECCG deck sections:

Tab Name Description
Pool Starting Pool Characters, starting items, and starter resources.
Res Resources Resource events, allies, factions, and playable items.
Haz Hazards Creatures, hazard events, and corruption cards.
Side Sideboard Reserve cards accessible during the game.
Site Sites Site cards and region movement paths.

4. Filter Bar (Bottom Panel)

Located beneath the three main panes, the filter panel is organized into two distinct, titled group boxes that provide fine-grained, context-sensitive faceted filtering. Each filter slot operates as a clear vertical column pair, ensuring you immediately know which control selects the category/attribute and which selects the specific value or tag:

  • Left Box — Card Attributes (Official Database): Contains two slots (Slots 1 & 2) for querying official card rules attributes synchronized from the Cardnum database.
    • Top Dropdown (Attribute): Selects the rules attribute (e.g., Primary, Alignment, Race, Skill, Mind, Prowess).
    • Bottom Dropdown (Value): Selects the specific value (e.g., Character, Hero, Dúnadan, Warrior).
  • Right Box — Custom Tags (User Taxonomy): Contains two slots (Slots 3 & 4) for querying your own classification categories and tags.
    • Top Dropdown (Category): Selects your user-defined category (e.g., Archetype, Role, Hazard Strategy).
    • Bottom Dropdown (Tag): Selects the specific custom tag (e.g., Ring Destruction, Scout Support, Anti-Fly).
Quick Filter Clearing: You can clear any filter slot by pressing Escape while focused inside it, right-clicking any filter box to choose Clear This Filter, or pressing Ctrl+R (or selecting Filter > Clear All Filters) to wipe all four filter pairs at once.

Dynamic Title Bar Summary

The window title updates automatically to reflect deck statistics:

MECCG Deck Builder - "[Deck Title]" (Pool/Res[Characters]/Haz/Side/Site)

For example: MECCG Deck Builder - "Ring Hunter" (5/30[4]/30/20/12) indicates 5 pool cards, 30 resource cards (including 4 characters), 30 hazards, 20 sideboard cards, and 12 sites.

Home > Sets & Filters

Sets & Filter Management

Managing Card Sets

Click the Set menu in the top bar to choose which expansions are active in the Master List. You can combine multiple sets at will:

  • Select All: Enables all official sets and Dreamcard expansions.
  • Clear All: Deselects all expansions.
  • Individual Sets: Check or uncheck individual expansions (e.g., The Wizards, The Dragons, Dark Minions, The Lidless Eye, The Balrog, or player council Dreamcard sets).

Dual-Layer Filtering Architecture

Located beneath the main workspace, four pairs of ComboBoxes provide fine-grained search and deck analysis. The bottom panel is partitioned into two clear GroupBoxes, with each filter slot arranged as a vertical column pair:

Filter Box & Slots Data Source Taxonomy Management Input Pairing
Left GroupBox:
Card Attributes (Official Database)
(Slots 1 & 2) 		Cardnum Open Database: Canonical card statistics synchronized from cardnum.net and GitHub, representing published cards from Iron Crown Enterprises (I.C.E.) and Council of Elrond Dreamcards. Fixed Attributes: Rules-based properties (Primary, Alignment, Race, Skill, Stats) are immutable. Vertical pair: Attribute dropdown above Value dropdown.
Right GroupBox:
Custom Tags (User Taxonomy)
(Slots 3 & 4) 		User-Defined Taxonomy: Managed locally in your deck builder session and saved to custom tag files (.json). Explicit Taxonomy Management: Create, rename, or delete categories and tags via Filter > Manage Custom Tags... or assign tags on the fly via the card context menu. Vertical pair: Category dropdown above Tag dropdown.

Cascading Faceted Search & Conflict Resolution

The filter system operates as an order-independent faceted search engine. All four slots continuously communicate with each other and with the active expansion set selections:

  • Context-Sensitive Value Pruning: The value dropdown for any slot only displays options present among cards that satisfy your active expansion sets and the other active filter slots. Selecting any choice from a dropdown is guaranteed to match at least one card, completely eliminating dead-end queries.
  • Order-Independent (Symmetric) Narrowing: You can choose filters in any order. For example, selecting Skill = Diplomat in Slot 2 first will automatically prune Slot 1's Secondary dropdown down to only card types that feature diplomats (Ally, Avatar, Character and Short-event).
  • Automatic Conflict Resolution: If an existing filter selection becomes impossible—such as deselecting an expansion in the Set menu or deleting a custom tag in the taxonomy manager—the invalid slot automatically and silently resets to blank ("").
  • Cross-Layer Integration: Custom tags in Slots 3 & 4 participate fully in faceting. Selecting a custom archetype (e.g., Archetype → Ring Destruction) will prune the Cardnum dropdowns (Slots 1 & 2) to only show primary types, races, and skills present on cards tagged with that archetype.
  • Expansion Set Pruning: Checking or unchecking sets in the Set menu dynamically recalculates available filter values. If all expansions are deselected, the master list and card image preview are cleared.

Cardnum Built-in Attributes (Slots 1 & 2)

The two left-hand selectors filter the catalog using official card attributes. Because these properties reflect canonical game rules, they are strictly read-only:

Attribute Name Typical Values
Primary Character, Resource, Hazard, Site, Region
Secondary Ally, Faction, Creature, Short-event, Long-event, Permanent-event, Minor Item, Major Item, Greater Item, etc.
Alignment Hero, Minion, Fallen-wizard, Balrog, Neutral
Race Dúnadan, Dwarf, Elf, Hobbit, Man, Wizard, Orc, Troll, Dragon
Skill Warrior, Scout, Ranger, Sage, Diplomat
Site / Region Free-hold, Border-hold, Ruins & Lairs, Shadow-hold, Dark-hold, Haven
Prowess / Body / Mind / MPs Numeric stats and victory point values
Multi-Skill Search: When searching by Skill, cards with compound skills (such as Warrior/Scout) are indexed by both terms individually.

Custom User Taxonomy (Slots 3 & 4)

The two right-hand slots allow you to filter cards by your own classification system (e.g., Archetype → Ring Destruction or Role → Scout Support). Authoring and managing tags is cleanly decoupled from filtering:

1. Managing the Taxonomy (Filter > Manage Custom Tags...)

Open Filter > Manage Custom Tags... to access the central tag management dialog. Here you can:

  • Add Categories: Create new classification categories (e.g., Archetype, Hazard Package, Role).
  • Rename Categories or Tags: Rename terms across your entire taxonomy; all tagged cards are updated automatically.
  • Add Tags: Add new tags under an existing category.
  • Delete Categories or Tags: Safely remove terms from the database and strip them from tagged cards.

2. Assigning Custom Tags to Cards

You can tag cards in the Master List or any Deck Tab using the context menu:

  • Assign or Reassign Existing Tag: Right-click a card and select Assign Tag > [Category] > [Tag]. The category menu displays a checkmark (✓) next to the currently assigned tag; selecting a different tag seamlessly updates and remaps the card.
  • Author and Assign New Tag: Right-click a card and select Assign Tag > [+ Author New Tag...]. This prompts for both category and tag, registers them into your taxonomy, and assigns them to the card in a single action without affecting your active filter bar.
  • Add New Tag to Existing Category: Right-click a card and select Assign Tag > [Category] > [+ Add Tag...] to author a new tag and assign it immediately.

3. Removing Tags from Cards

  • Remove Tag from Single Card: Right-click the card and choose Remove Tag > [Category] > [Tag]. The tag is unassigned from that card, but remains in your taxonomy for other cards.
  • Delete Globally: Use Filter > Manage Custom Tags... to permanently delete a category or tag across all cards in the catalog.

4. Saving and Loading Custom Tag Sets

  • Filter > Save Tag Set...: Exports your entire custom taxonomy and all card tag assignments to a portable .json file.
  • Filter > Load Tag Set...: Loads a previously saved custom tag set, restoring all categories, tags, and card mappings.

Clearing and Resetting Filters

Method Shortcut / Gesture Scope & Behavior
Global Reset Menu: Filter > Clear All Filters
Keyboard: Ctrl+R 		Instantly resets all four filter slots (Slots 1–4) to blank and refreshes the master card list.
Slot Context Menu Right-Click any of the 8 filter ComboBoxes Opens a context menu with options to:
  • Clear This Filter: Resets both the category/attribute and value of that specific slot to blank.
  • Clear All Filters: Resets all four slots at once.
Quick Keyboard Reset Escape When focused inside any category or tag ComboBox, pressing Escape immediately resets that box to the blank ("") entry.
Manual Dropdown Reset Select the top blank entry ("") Selecting the empty item at the top of any category dropdown resets that slot and clears its paired tag list.

Home > Tools & Image Cache

Tools & Image Cache Architecture

Card Artwork Cache System

The application employs a two-tier caching architecture:

  1. Memory Cache: An in-memory cache holding up to 10,000 active Bitmaps for instant display when scrolling or clicking.
  2. Local Disk Cache: Whenever a card image is requested, the application checks for an existing image on disk under a folder matching the set code (e.g., METW/metw_adrazar.jpg).
    • If found locally, the image loads immediately with zero network latency.
    • If not found, it downloads from Cardnum, saves a copy into the set folder, and stores it in memory.

Batch Image Downloader

If you plan to use MECCG Deck Builder offline (e.g., on a laptop during tournaments or travel), you can pre-download card images:

  1. Enable all sets you want cached via the Set menu.
  2. Reset your filters so that all cards are listed in the Master List.
  3. Select Tools > Download Images.
Note: The batch downloader runs asynchronously in the background with real-time progress reported in the window title bar, ensuring the application remains responsive while saving each card image to disk.

Offline Data Fallbacks

The builder is resilient against network outages:

  • Cards: Automatically attempts to download the latest card definitions from Cardnum on launch. If offline or unavailable, it seamlessly falls back to the bundled local cards-dc.json file.
  • Sets: Automatically attempts to download the latest expansion set metadata. If offline, it reads the bundled local sets-dc.json file.

# Coding Standards & Guidelines: MECCG Deck Builder
## 1. General Principles - Modern .NET Standard: Target C# 12 / .NET 8 idioms (collection expressions [], pattern matching, nullability annotations). - Separation of Concerns: Keep UI presentation (Form1.cs) strictly separated from domain logic, file I/O, network access, and deck generation algorithms. Forms should act as views, delegating logic to dedicated services or models. - Fail-Safe & User-Friendly: Catch exceptions gracefully, report actionable messages to the user, and never let unhandled background exceptions crash the UI thread.
---
## 2. Naming Conventions
### Identifiers - Classes, Records, Enums, Structs, Methods, Properties: Use PascalCase. - Examples: CardCatalog, GenerateDeck(), DeckTitle - Local Variables, Method Parameters, Private Fields: Use camelCase. - Examples: cardIndex, selectedSet, filePath - Private / Internal Class Fields: Prefix with an underscore _ or use standard camelCase. - Examples: _cards, _httpClient (or cards, s_httpClient for static instances). - Constants: Use PascalCase. - Examples: CardnumCardsUrl, PoolFileSuffix (avoid ALL_CAPS). - Event Handlers in WinForms: Use ControlName_EventName in PascalCase. - Examples: ContentsToolStripMenuItem_Click, ListBoxMaster_SelectedIndexChanged - Note: Ensure the control name starts with an uppercase letter to satisfy Roslyn rule IDE1006.
---
## 3. Architecture & Domain Modeling
### Strongly-Typed Models over Raw Arrays - No More string[] for Entities: Replace List<string[]> and SortedDictionary<string, string> with strongly-typed records or classes (e.g., Card, DeckCard, DeckSection). - Enums for Domain Constants: Use strongly-typed enums for fixed concepts (e.g., DeckSection.Pool, DeckSection.Resources, CardAlignment.Hero). - Immutability Where Appropriate: Card catalog definitions should be read-only once loaded into memory.
### Headless & Testable Domain Logic - Deck export routines, deck import routines, card filtering, and the future procedural deck generator must never take ListBox, ComboBox, or Form controls as parameters. - Operate on pure domain structures (e.g., Deck, IEnumerable<Card>, FilterCriteria) so they can be tested via unit tests and run headless.
---
## 4. Asynchronous Programming & Threading
### No Blocking on Async Tasks - Never use .Result, .Wait(), or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() on the UI thread. - All network requests (HttpClient) and disk I/O should use async / await: - Avoid: string json = s_httpClient.GetStringAsync(url).Result; - Prefer: string json = await s_httpClient.GetStringAsync(url); - Long-running batch operations (such as Download Images or Generate Deck) must be performed asynchronously or on a background task (Task.Run) with progress updates via IProgress<T> or Progress<int>.
---
## 5. Resource Management & GDI+ Safety
### Safe Image Loading (No File Locking) - Never instantiate new Bitmap(filePath) directly for files that might be overwritten or deleted, as GDI+ keeps the file locked indefinitely. - Instead, read the image bytes into a MemoryStream and create an independent Bitmap clone: - Read bytes via File.ReadAllBytes(filePath) - Copy into MemoryStream - Construct Bitmap from stream and return an independent instance.
### Disposal of GDI+ Objects - When assigning a new image to PictureBox.Image, always dispose of the previous image if it is an unmanaged, uncached copy to prevent GDI object leaks. - Always dispose Graphics, Pen, Brush, and Font objects using using statements.
---
## 6. Encodings & String Formats
- Internal Strings: Standard .NET UTF-16 strings. - JSON Serialization: Use UTF-8 without BOM (System.Text.Json or Newtonsoft.Json). - Legacy Play MECCG Files (.play): Explicitly specify Windows-1252 ANSI: - Encoding.GetEncoding(1252) - HTML Help Files (.hhp, .hhc, .hhk): Must be saved as ANSI (Windows-1252) or UTF-8 without BOM/signature. Never save help project files with a UTF-8 BOM.
---
## 7. Error Handling & Defensive Coding
- No Silent Exception Swallowing: Avoid empty catch (Exception) { } blocks. At minimum, log the error or provide user feedback via a status bar or message box. - Specific Exception Catching: Catch specific exceptions (e.g., HttpRequestException, JsonException, IOException) before general Exception. - Collection Key Safety: Use TryGetValue() or ContainsKey() before accessing dictionaries to prevent KeyNotFoundException.
---
## 8. Formatting & Tooling - Indentation: 4 spaces (no tabs in C# source files; tabs permitted only in generated export templates if required by format specification like Tabletop Simulator JSON). - Line Endings: CRLF (\r\n) for Windows compatibility. - Warnings as Errors: Aim for zero compiler warnings and zero Roslyn analyzer warnings on Release builds.

# MECCG Deck Builder
An offline-capable Windows desktop application for building, organizing, filtering, and exporting decks for the **Middle-earth Collectible Card Game (MECCG)** by Iron Crown Enterprises (I.C.E.), including official expansions and Council of Elrond Dreamcard sets.
---
## Features
- **Complete Card Database:** Automatically synchronizes card and set definitions from the open Cardnum database, with offline local JSON fallback. - **Five-Section Deck Partitions:** Manage cards across standard competitive partitions: - **Pool:** Starting company, starter items, and opening resources. - **Resources:** Resource events, allies, factions, and items. - **Hazards:** Creatures, hazard events, and corruption. - **Sideboard:** Sideboard reserves. - **Sites:** Sites and movement regions. - **Dynamic Stats Summary:** Window title bar displays live card counts per section with dedicated character counts: `(Pool / Res [Characters] / Haz / Side / Site)`. - **Card Artwork Preview & Caching:** On-demand card artwork download from Cardnum with local disk caching (`METW/`, `MEDM/`, etc.) and an in-memory cache. ICE errata cards load corrected artwork automatically. - **Dual-Layer Filtering:** - **Official Card Attributes (Slots 1 & 2):** Filter by Primary type, Alignment, Race, Skills, Stats, Unique status, Sites, and more. - **Custom User Taxonomy (Slots 3 & 4):** Filter by custom categories and tags (e.g., `Archetype` -> `Ring Destruction`, `Role` -> `Scout Support`). Author tags via the dedicated **Manage Custom Tags** dialog or right-click **Assign Tag > [+ Author New Tag...]** without disturbing active filter criteria. - **Multi-Platform Export Formats:** - **Tabletop Simulator (`.json`):** Generates ready-to-use deck files compatible with TTS MECCG mods. - **Play MECCG (`.play` & `.playPBEM`):** Native format for online play. - **Cardnum Deck (`.cnum`):** Standard `1 <Code>` listing format. - **Archive Breakdown (`.archive`):** Categorized breakdown (Items, Events, Characters by race, Sites by type). - **Plain Text (`.txt`):** Formatted deck listing.
---
## Keyboard & Mouse Shortcuts
| Action | Location | Behavior | |---|---|---| | Left Click | Master List | Select card and preview image | | Double Click | Master List | Add card to the active deck tab | | Double Click | Any Deck Tab | Duplicate the clicked card in that tab | | Drag & Drop | Master List -> Tab | Add card to the target tab | | Right Click | Master List | Context menu: Copy to tab, view Card Attributes, view Assigned Tags, assign custom tags | | Right Click | Deck Tab | Context menu: Copy, Move to another tab, Delete, view Card Attributes / Tags | | Right Click | Filter ComboBox | Context menu: Clear this filter slot or clear all filters | | Escape | Filter ComboBox | Reset focused filter ComboBox to blank | | Ctrl + N | Global | Start a new deck | | Ctrl + O | Global | Open saved deck (`.json`) | | Ctrl + S | Global | Export deck dialog | | Ctrl + R | Global | Clear all active filter slots |

## Getting Started
### Prerequisites - Windows 10 / 11 - .NET 8.0 Desktop Runtime (or Visual Studio 2022 v17.8+)
### Building from Source 1. Clone the repository: ```bash git clone https://github.com/davidk64fnq/MECCG-Deck-Builder.git cd MECCG-Deck-Builder ```
2. Restore packages and build: ```bash dotnet restore dotnet build -c Release ```
3. Run the executable in `bin/Release/net8.0-windows/MECCG Deck Builder.exe`.
---
## Offline Use & Image Pre-downloading To pre-cache card artwork for tournament or offline use: 1. Open the application. 2. Under the **Set** menu, check the sets you wish to cache. 3. Select **Tools > Download Images**. Card artwork will download to local set folders.
---
